claim: Acceptance criterion 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured' is not met. When no SurrogateType is given, `Collect` always calls `CreateContractlessMembers(type)`, which reads no attributes on T. As a result, `[MessagePackObject]`, `[Key(int)]`, `[Key(string)]`, `keyAsPropertyName`, `[IgnoreMember]`, `[DataContract]`, `[DataMember]` and `[IgnoreDataMember]` on T are all ignored. Every public readable member is written as a string-keyed map entry. An int-keyed T is therefore serialized as a map instead of an array, and ignored members are serialized. That is a different wire format from the formatter the attributes describe. `[Union]` on T is rejected with MsgPack021 (abstract/interface) rather than honoured.

claim: The requirement says MessagePack attributes on T must be honoured if present. GeneratedFormatterCollector never reads T's attributes. Without a surrogate, CreateContractlessMembers serializes every public readable member, even when T marks it [IgnoreMember] or [IgnoreDataMember]. [MessagePackObject], [Key] and [DataContract]/[DataMember(Name=...)] on T are ignored as well, so the wire format differs from what T declares. [DataContract]/[DataMember] is the realistic case: Project A can use it without referencing MessagePack.

claim: Contractless members are sorted by name with ordinal comparison and int keys assigned by index. DynamicContractlessObjectResolver orders members differently (declaration order with base-first). The requirement says contractless behaviour; wire bytes from generated formatter may differ in map key order from the dynamic contractless formatter, and in what is serialized (read-only members written as serialize-only). Users switching from reflection-based contractless to this would see different byte ordering.

claim: The generated formatter is emitted without regard to MessagePackSecurity. Contractless string-key deserialization of an attacker-controlled external type relies on the generated StringKey template. If that template builds a dictionary or span lookup of keys, a hash-collision-resistant comparer is not involved. The generator also never routes the generated map and array reads through options.Security.DepthStep. The generated formatter for a type with nested members must call DepthStep. Nothing in the diff checks that this holds for the user-declared formatter path.
